# Transcription

## Page 1

**Northbridge Lettings**
**Check-out inspection report**

Record the condition, cleanliness, contents, defects and photographic evidence observed during a check-out inspection at Flat 8, 168 Alder Lane, Kingshaven, ZZ4 3ZZ.

Check-out report. Appointment date: 25 August 2026. Assessor: Northbridge Lettings.

The assessor confirms that the report reflects their assessment of the property. Signature received: 27 September 2025 14:00:39.

The report describes the main features of the property room by room and records observed defects with photographs. The inspection was visual; inaccessible and loft areas were not inspected. Fixtures and fittings may not have been tested. The report does not provide repair advice or costs and may not identify structural defects.

The report guidance states that at the end of a tenancy the property and contents are expected to be in a similar condition and cleanliness to the start-of-tenancy report. Damage beyond fair wear and tear may require repair or replacement, with costs potentially deducted from the tenant's deposit. Unsatisfactory cleaning may require professional cleaning, with costs potentially deducted from the deposit. Receipts for repair, replacement or professional cleaning should be retained if required.

The report guidance says the property should be left tidy and cleaning thorough. It refers to cleaning carpets and curtains as required by the agreement; leaving vinyl or tile flooring clean and free from cracks or tears; maintaining decor and repairing added picture hooks, nails, screws or screw holes; removing excessive marks and fingerprints; defrosting, switching off and leaving refrigerators and freezers open; cleaning ovens, hobs, extractor units and microwaves; and tidying gardens where applicable.

The report guidance states smoke and carbon monoxide alarms will have been checked and working as of the report date, and that tenants are responsible for keeping them in working order during the tenancy. Faults other than battery replacement should be reported immediately.

Condition rating guidance: Excellent means unused or new; Good means minor wear with no obvious appearance or function faults; Fair means wear or minor damage; Poor means extensive wear such as stains, marks, rips or chips; Unacceptable means not fit for purpose, badly damaged or faulty.

Cleanliness rating guidance for inspection areas: Excellent means cleaned to a high standard; Good means cleaned to a good standard; Fair means cleaned to a fair standard; Poor means light cleaning is required; Unacceptable means professional cleaning is required. For item cleanliness, Fair, Poor and Unacceptable ratings direct the reader to the issues and photographs.

Lounge description: Double sofa; grey carpets; off-white coloured walls; all clean and in good order. Two spotlights not working. Cieling tile water damage. Maintenance.

Bedroom description: 3/4 bed with mattress protector; double wardrobe; TV on wall bracket; remote; table and chair. All in good clean order.

Bathroom description: Walk-in shower and screen; towel rail radiator; toilet; toilet brush; sink on vanity unit; small wall mirror. Room is not clean and some items left. Items left. Cleaning required.

Assessor declaration: The report reflects the assessor's assessment of the property.

input.message:
Dear Landlord,

Re: Flat 8, 168 Alder Lane, Kingshaven, ZZ4 3ZZ – ref R/PM007-1 (Job NBL-007-0235)

Following the check-out inspection, the lounge has two spotlights not working and a ceiling tile with water damage. We asked our contractor, Clarke, to quote, and he has quoted £198.37 plus VAT (£238.04 including VAT at 20%) to replace the two spotlights and one ceiling board.

Please note the quote covers replacing the damaged board only; the report does not say what caused the water damage. If you would like the contractor to check for an active leak above the ceiling while attending, please let us know.

Reply APPROVE to go ahead with the quote of £198.37 + VAT, or DECLINE if you do not wish to proceed.

Kind regards,
Donna
Northbridge Lettings – Maintenance

data.reasoning: I notice the appointment date says 2026 but the signature says 2025, which is likely a typo worth flagging. The ceiling water damage could point to an underlying leak issue, and there may be deposit deduction questions tied to the quote, though that's outside scope. The quote needs landlord approval by email, but since approval was already recorded before the quote without an amount and is already marked approved, I don't think a new approval request is needed.

result.summary: Clarke has quoted £198.37 + VAT (£238.04 if VAT is 20%) for the lounge spotlights and ceiling board. The only landlord approval on file is a system note with no amount, logged before any quote existed. So I emailed the landlord the quote and asked them to reply APPROVE or DECLINE. I also told Clarke the quote is with the landlord and asked him not to book any work yet. A hold is set to chase the landlord in 2 days.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 001/005 was a request for a quote, not an instruction to do the work. The approval in event 002 (approval id 7) was logged automatically 5 seconds after the ticket was created. It has no amount and came before the quote. No spend limit is recorded for the landlord, so the £198.37 + VAT quote in event 008 isn't clearly covered. Committing that money without the landlord seeing the figure would break the rule against spending a landlord's money without approval. Event 007 asked whether the provider needs a reply: yes, a short note to say the quote has been received and work shouldn't start yet.

alternatives_considered.why_not: That approval has no amount and came before the quote. With no spend limit on file, committing £238 would mean spending the landlord's money without approval.
Nothing conflicts or is disputed. Getting the landlord's approval is the normal next step, and I can do that myself.
